text: Training loss at a single parameter vector can conceal differences in test performance among minima. Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) instead minimizes worst-case loss in a weight neighborhood with weight regularization, favoring solutions whose nearby parameters also have low loss. A PAC-Bayesian bound motivates this objective when Gaussian perturbations do not reduce population loss and the parameter norm is at least one; it does not certify the practical approximation. SAM perturbs weights along the gradient and updates using the perturbed-weight gradient, dropping second-order terms and requiring two backpropagations. On CIFAR-10/100, gains over baselines allowed up to twice as many epochs support benefits beyond longer pointwise training: AutoAugment WideResNet reduces CIFAR-10 error from 2.2% to 1.6%. ImageNet training and pretrained EfficientNet finetuning also improve. Clean-test accuracy improves under random label corruption, but SAM trails MentorMix; bootstrapping narrows the gap without eliminating it at the highest noise rate. Complementary analyses find lower Hessian curvature and show that separate neighborhood maximizations on smaller subsets improve SAM generalization and make m-sharpness more predictive of generalization gaps in the studied settings. These diagnostics support neighborhood-based optimization without establishing curvature as the isolated cause, and an augmented SVHN configuration worsens.

Similar training losses can conceal different generalization performance, so Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) targets low loss throughout a parameter neighborhood. A conditional PAC-Bayesian bound motivates worst-case neighborhood-loss minimization, assuming Gaussian perturbations do not reduce population loss and weight norm is at least one. The practical optimizer constructs a loss-increasing perturbation from one gradient, then updates the original weights using a second gradient at the perturbed weights. CIFAR models trained from scratch improve across all tested configurations despite non-SAM baselines being allowed twice as many epochs: AutoAugment WideResNet CIFAR-10 error falls from 2.2% to 1.6%. Gains on ImageNet ResNets and EfficientNet finetuning after ImageNet or ImageNet-plus-JFT pretraining extend this evidence beyond one training regime. Lower Hessian curvature in the tested model supports the intended neighborhood geometry, without establishing a generalization guarantee for approximate updates. With random label noise, SAM improves clean-test accuracy over SGD but trails MentorMix without bootstrapping; an augmented SVHN configuration also worsens. A complementary m-sharpness analysis maximizes loss separately over data subsets: smaller subsets tend to improve generalization and better predict generalization gaps in the evaluated settings, making subset size consequential rather than an implementation detail.

VoxPoser turns language-specified manipulation subtasks into spatial objectives by assigning voxel values that attract an end-effector, object, or object part toward goals and repel it from obstacles. Generated programs query visual perception to ground these maps, letting motion planners optimize desired motion and constraints jointly instead of requiring language models to specify action parameters directly. Observation-based replanning enables zero-shot execution without additional training. Across five real-world tasks, success is 88% in static scenes and 70% under disturbances, versus 24% and 0% for an LLM using simple primitives, supporting spatial composition over sequential primitive specification. Across 13 simulated tasks, category averages favor VoxPoser on seen and unseen instructions and attributes, although individual tasks favor baselines. For three simulated contact-rich tasks, synthesized trajectories also restrict exploration to locally perturbed waypoints: online dynamics learning raises success from 3.3-18.3% to 80.0-91.7% with mean interaction times below three minutes, while exploration without priors exceeds 12 hours. This contrast supports task-directed adaptation when zero-shot plans are insufficient; perception errors, restricted environment dynamics, and end-effector-only planning delimit the demonstrated capabilities.

VoxPoser turns language-specified manipulation goals into trajectory objectives: pretrained language models generate programs that query perception and assign voxel values attracting an end-effector or object toward targets while discouraging constraint violations. Scoring trajectories against these spatial objectives lets a planner consider goals and constraints jointly instead of encoding them only as primitive sequences, and replan from updated observations without additional training. Across five tabletop robot tasks, success averages 88% without disturbances and 70% with disturbances, versus 24% and 0% for a language-model-plus-primitives baseline, supporting spatial planning for tasks and disruptions that primitive sequencing handles poorly. In 13 simulated tasks, category-level gains over this baseline and learned costmaps extend to unseen instructions and attributes, but individual tasks do not uniformly improve. For contact-intensive simulated door, window, and fridge tasks, zero-shot trajectories are insufficient yet provide exploration priors: sampling near them concentrates interactions around task-relevant motions, enabling dynamics learning with under three minutes of online interaction versus exceeding a twelve-hour limit without priors. Perception and environment dynamics limit performance; prompts remain manually engineered, and planning covers the end-effector rather than the whole arm.
